topic.title: The 90-day notice is a cage, not a handover
topic.claim: Companies keep a 90-day notice period because it kills your next offer, not because handover takes three months.
topic.moment: The recruiter's voice going flat when you say 'my notice is ninety days'.

turn.believed: Long notice periods exist so work can be handed over properly.
turn.actually: They make you expensive to hire, so you stay where you are.

topic.because: A new employer won't wait three months for most roles. The old one keeps you without paying a rupee more.
topic.payoff: Ask HR how many people have actually served the full ninety days. The answer tells you what it's for.
topic.behaviour: Firms set long notice periods, then offer buyouts or early release only when it suits them.
topic.mechanism: A long exit raises the cost of hiring you, which lowers your bargaining power.
topic.send_to: The friend who lost an offer because they couldn't join in 30 days.
topic.why_now: Hiring has slowed, and companies are holding on harder to the people they have.

score.why: The 90-day notice period is built to kill your next offer, not for handover; the flat recruiter voice is a real scene.

topic.villain: a notice-period policy designed to make you too expensive for anyone else to hire
